blindComparison: A stranger picks Ghost of Tsushima, and the reason is graphic structure at magic hour, not detail count. In Tsushima's golden-hour frames the sky is doing work — a graded blue-to-ember vertical gradient with real cloud structure — and every object between the camera and the sun collapses to a near-black silhouette with a hot rim. In our set the sky is a flat card in three of five frames (torii zenith->horizon 146.1 -> 165.4, a 19-code monotone ramp, per-box lumaSpread 3.1-4.8; valley anti-solar RGB [178.9,186.4,180.1], saturation 0.040, and green-shifted, G-B = +6.3), and near the sun everything goes to milk instead of silhouette (a 152x47 box at (1393,644) in `sun` containing a stone lantern, a fence and a treeline reads p50 226.1, detail 0.60, lumaSpread 26.7). Tsushima's frame has a dark half and a light half; ours has a pale half and a muddy half. Second, at 1:1 our hero frame has literal black holes in the floor: an irregular hard-edged patch at (1413,989) reads RGB [2.9,3.0,4.0] against neighbouring flagstone [53.6,42.0,39.0] two metres away. No shipped title has that in a marketing frame.

findings.problem: Large irregular near-black patches lie on the lit flagstone plaza in the near foreground, with hard boundaries and no interior detail. Measured: box (1413,989 51x23) inside the patch left of the stone lantern reads meanRGB [2.9,3.0,4.0], luma p50 3.1, detail 2.54. Neighbouring flagstone of the same material 160 px away, box (1253,989 51x23), reads meanRGB [53.6,42.0,39.0], luma p50 43.1, detail 8.50. That is 7.2% of its neighbour in sRGB and roughly 0.12x in linear. A second patch of the same kind sits immediately right of the same lantern: box (1557,989 38x18) reads meanRGB [4.5,4.9,6.3], p50 3.9. The patches are amoeba-shaped, have no caster above them, are not puddles (a wet-stone puddle under a sky at luma 165-190 cannot be at code 3 — Fresnel alone would put the sky in it), and they delete the ground texture entirely inside their boundary. Crop to see it: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-hero-r16.png 0.50,0.79,0.20,0.16`. The same defect family is visible across the wide plateau.
findings.why: A hole in the floor in the foreground of the hero frame is the single most disqualifying thing in the set. It reads as a rendering error, not as art — no amount of surrounding quality survives it, and it is exactly what a stranger's eye lands on first in a side-by-side.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING — DISPROVE BEFORE ACTING. Something is subtracting illumination rather than reflectance in these regions: round 15 established the patch is 4x darker than the darkest reflectance Materials.js can produce, so it is not albedo. Candidates worth an ablation each: a negative or over-ranged local light/occlusion volume; a shadow-map term evaluating to a large negative before clamp; an AO or decal term applied multiplicatively more than once. Do NOT re-open cascade coverage — rounds 8 and 15 disproved that three times and the instruction stands that nobody should touch cascade code for this.
findings.fix: Eliminate the near-black patches so no region of the plaza falls below the surrounding material's fill floor. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: `probe stats shots/phone-hero-rN.png 0.558,0.845,0.020,0.020` must return luma p50 >= 0.55 x the p50 of `probe stats ... 0.495,0.845,0.020,0.020` (i.e. >= ~24 if the neighbour is still ~43), and detail >= 5.0 in the same box (the ground texture must be visible inside it, not just lifted). Same pair of conditions for the second patch at 0.615,0.845,0.015,0.015. GUARD against faking this with a global lift: the neighbouring-flagstone box 0.495,0.845,0.020,0.020 must stay within +/-8% of its current p50 43.1, and whole-frame `probe stats ... 0,0,1,1` must stay within +/-5% of its current luma p50 75.3 and p1 2.7.

findings.problem: There are no volumetric shafts anywhere in the two frames the contract names (ARCHITECTURE 5, non-negotiable #4: 'volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo'). What the pass delivers is a smooth radial glow plus a global wash. Evidence, using an explicit low-frequency profile because `detail` cannot see a shaft: (a) an arc of 16x16 probe boxes at r=330 px around the sun disc at (1528,538) in `sun`, restricted to the open-sky sector 60deg-110deg, gives luma p50 211.8, 216.5, 231.8, 230.8, 220.0, 190.2 — strictly unimodal, zero angular local minima or maxima, so no bar structure at any angle. (b) a horizontal run of 24x24 boxes across the backlit bamboo in `valley` at y=386 from x=500 to x=1100 gives 116.7, 121.2, 121.6, 123.3, 130.0, 126.1, 139.8, 141.2, 146.1, 141.7, 147.4, 156.6, 153.7, 156.7, 154.7, 155.5, 154.5, 147.0, 150.8, 156.4, 158.7, 156.7, 155.7, 171.7, 169.7, 168.4 — a monotone rise toward the sun with a maximum deviation from trend of ~7 code values. No shafts. (c) What the eye reads as a fan of rays in `sun` at native is solid shide geometry, not light: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-sun-r16.png 0.47,0.03,0.21,0.40`. The other half of the same defect is the wash it substitutes: a 152x47 box at (1393,644) containing a stone lantern, a fence rail and the treeline reads p50 226.1, saturation 0.191, detail 0.60, lumaSpread 26.7 — the entire mid-field within roughly 15deg of the sun is erased to a flat cream card, so the lantern that should be the strongest silhouette in the frame is a ghost.
findings.why: Backlit shafts through a torii are the signature image of this genre and they are a binding contract item. Worse, the substitute is actively harmful: it inverts the contrast that makes Tsushima and Sekiro read. In the reference, objects near the sun go to near-black with a hot rim; here they go to milk, so the frame loses its graphic skeleton exactly where it should be strongest.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 15 established the emitter is not empty (rtGodA 10.2-11.0% non-zero with uprights, shimenawa, shide and bamboo present) and that undersampling is not the limit (converged by N=48). It also established that the god-ray finding and the mid-field-wash finding are one defect, and that the correct direction is LESS SPREAD, NOT MORE GAIN — raising the weight is the round-7 regression and it made the frame worse. So the hunch to test first is that the radial blur/decay footprint is wide enough that a 10%-coverage emitter is being spread to near-full-frame coverage, converting a differential signal into common mode. Test it by measuring the coverage of the pass output before and after narrowing the footprint, not by changing gain.
findings.fix: Make the pass differential: discrete shafts where occluders sit, and no contribution where they do not. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame, using the same arc apparatus: on an arc of 16x16 boxes at r=330 px around the measured sun disc, stepping 5deg through the open-sky sector 55deg-115deg, the luma p50 sequence must contain at least 3 local maxima and 3 local minima with peak-to-trough >= 18 code values, i.e. it must stop being unimodal. GUARD 1 against faking with gain: the arc's mean p50 over that sector must stay within +/-6% of its current 216.9. GUARD 2, this is the important one: the mid-field must come back, so `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.55,0.55,0.06,0.04` must return detail >= 3.5 (currently 0.60) and luma p50 <= 205 (currently 226.1) with lumaSpread >= 60 (currently 26.7), while whole-frame p50 stays within +/-6% of 163.3. GUARD 3: the clean-sky control `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.05,0.03,0.06,0.04` must not gain shaft structure — its lumaSpread must stay below 15.

findings.problem: The sky is a flat, near-achromatic card in three of five frames, and it is not magic hour in any of them. Vertical profile in `torii`, 203x47 boxes at x=1772: zenith (y=23) meanRGB [122.8,151.2,166.8] sat 0.264 p50 146.1; mid (y=211) [132.6,159.9,171.9] sat 0.229 p50 155.0; horizon (y=421) [146.6,169.9,175.9] sat 0.166 p50 165.4. That is a 19-code monotone ramp across the entire visible sky, with per-box lumaSpread 3.1/3.8/4.8 and detail 0.76/0.58/0.46 — mathematically a plain card. `hero` column at x=1152 runs p50 165.3, 169.2, 172.3, 176.4, 179.8, 186.5, 184.5, 189.3 from y=12 to y=339: 24 codes, saturation falling 0.187 -> 0.084, again lumaSpread 3.9-8.7. Worst case is `valley`, where the anti-solar sky at (2228,23 152x47) reads meanRGB [178.9,186.4,180.1] at saturation 0.040 with G > R > B — a literally colourless, faintly green sky opposite a low sun. There is no warm horizon band on the sun side, no deep blue at zenith, no cloud with any density, and no colour-temperature change anywhere across the dome.
findings.why: The setting is stated as magic hour, and the sky is the single largest surface in three of these frames. Tsushima's golden hour earns most of its impression from a sky that is doing colour work; a pale monotone card behind an otherwise decent shrine reads as a placeholder skybox and drags the whole set to 'tech demo' on first glance, before a viewer notices anything else.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 15 measured that this is not a round-15 regression and not caused by aerial perspective (removing 100% of aerial perspective moved the affected boxes by 0.1 code value), and that switching bloom and god rays off moved sky-adjacent saturation 0.188 -> 0.348. So part of what flattens the sky may be the same common-mode wash as the god-ray finding, and the two owners should compare notes before either concludes. The part that is Sky.js's alone to prove or disprove is whether the dome itself, sampled before post, already has this little chroma and this little vertical structure.
findings.fix: Deliver a magic-hour sky with real vertical and azimuthal colour structure. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: (1) `torii` vertical profile at x-frac 0.70, boxes 0.08x0.04 at y-frac 0.02 / 0.18 / 0.36 must span >= 45 code values of luma p50 end to end (currently 19) AND the zenith box saturation must be >= 0.38 (currently 0.264). (2) `valley` anti-solar box `probe stats shots/phone-valley-rN.png 0.88,0.02,0.06,0.04` must return saturation >= 0.22 (currently 0.040) with B > G (currently G exceeds B by 6.3) — it must be blue, not grey. (3) The sun-side sky must be warmer than the anti-solar sky by a measurable amount: in `valley`, mean R/B of box 0.06,0.02,0.06,0.04 minus mean R/B of box 0.88,0.02,0.06,0.04 must be >= 0.25 (currently 1.229 - 0.993 = 0.236, marginal). GUARD against a global saturation or contrast move: whole-frame `probe stats shots/phone-torii-rN.png 0,0,1,1` must stay within +/-6% of its current luma p50 112.1 and within +/-0.04 of its current saturation 0.334, and the flagstone control box `probe stats shots/phone-torii-rN.png 0.45,0.88,0.06,0.04` must stay within +/-8% of its current mean RGB.

findings.problem: The sakura canopy is built from large, flat-shaded, hard-alpha-cut cards with no petal-scale detail. At native the individual blossom clusters are 45-75 px angular polygons on a crown that spans ~700 px, i.e. each single 'blossom' is roughly a tenth of the whole tree, and each is a smooth untextured facet bounded by a hard binary alpha edge with no partial coverage. Crop to see it: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-hero-r16.png 0.16,0.06,0.10,0.14` (253x164 at 1:1). The shading is also bimodal rather than continuous: lit cards at (463,111 51x29) read meanRGB [158.9,83.7,85.3] saturation 0.483, shadowed cards at (284,269 51x35) read [99.5,75.3,92.1] saturation 0.265 with B exceeding G by 22%, so the same tree carries a salmon population and a mauve population with nothing between them.
findings.why: The tree is the only warm-coloured mass in the hero frame's left third and the eye goes straight to it. At 1:1 it reads as chunks of coloured card, which immediately tells a viewer the foliage is billboards. Tsushima's blossom reads as a cloud of small petals with soft coverage at the silhouette; ours reads as confetti glued to a branch.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Two independent candidates, each cheap to ablate: (a) the blossom card is being instanced at a world size several times larger than a real cluster, so a correct texture is simply magnified past its detail; (b) the card material is alpha-tested with no alpha-to-coverage/dither, so the silhouette is binary at every scale. Measure card world size and alpha mode before changing either.
findings.fix: Break the canopy into petal-scale elements with soft silhouette coverage. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: in `probe stats shots/phone-hero-rN.png 0.112,0.230,0.020,0.030` and `0.150,0.280,0.020,0.030` the detail must rise to >= 12.0 (currently 5.69 and 8.15) — real petal structure is high-frequency and detail is the right instrument for it. Additionally, the largest single flat-shaded facet in the crop `0.16,0.06,0.10,0.14` must be under 25 px across at native. GUARD against faking with grain or sharpening: the two boxes' meanRGB must each stay within +/-8% per channel of their current values, and whole-frame detail on `hero` must stay within +/-15% of its current 5.90 (a global sharpen would move it much more).

findings.problem: The two foreground torii uprights are untextured flat-shaded surfaces, in direct violation of ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #9 ('No untextured flat-colour surfaces anywhere in frame. Everything has grain.'). The right-hand upright spans native x=1720 to x=2070 — 350 px, 13.8% of the frame width — and is the nearest object in the shot. A horizontal run of 20x20 boxes at y=597 across it gives luma p50 200.5, 189.9, 176.7, 163.9, 148.5, 134.8, 124.7, 114.6, 103.3, 93.9, 86.8, 79.7, 76.7, 73.2: a strictly monotone Lambert ramp with zero local structure over 350 px. Mean |Laplacian| on the post is 1.48 at (1823,234 127x140) and 1.88 at (1823,819 127x140); the centre upright is 1.66 at (1190,234 46x140). The plaza in the same frame reads 7.3-10.6 and the stone lantern post reads 9.26, so this is not a global softness — it is these props. Crop: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-sun-r16.png 0.68,0.25,0.14,0.24` shows a plain orange-brown gradient with no wood fibre, no lacquer variation, no node or joint, no bevel highlight.
findings.why: It is the largest and closest thing in the frame. A hero-scale prop with a pure Lambert gradient and no grain is the clearest single 'untextured placeholder' signal in the set, and no shipped title would ship a foreground column like this.
findings.fix: Give the torii uprights real surface at the scale they occupy: vertical wood fibre, lacquer wear, and node/joint breakup. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.72,0.20,0.05,0.12` and `0.72,0.70,0.05,0.12` must each return detail >= 6.5 (currently 1.48 and 1.88), and the horizontal run of 20x20 boxes at y-frac 0.51 across x=1720..2070 must contain at least 4 local minima with a >= 10-code dip against the smooth Lambert trend. GUARD against faking with global grain or sharpening: the two boxes' meanRGB must each stay within +/-6% per channel of their current [158.6,97.7,55.8] and [123.5,69.8,37.9], the plaza control `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.20,0.85,0.06,0.04` must stay within +/-15% of its current detail, and whole-frame detail on `sun` must stay within +/-20% of its current 3.11.

findings.problem: In the widest establishing shot, the plateau — the largest surface in the frame and the lower 55% of it — carries no key light at all, and is net blue-shifted at magic hour. A row of ten 101x35 boxes at y=725 spanning the full frame width gives meanRGB: x=127 [44.4,49.1,50.2]; x=380 [44.7,48.1,49.0]; x=633 [40.8,45.0,46.4]; x=886 [62.2,56.4,55.9]; x=1139 [120.1,79.3,66.0] (a lantern pool, excluded); x=1393 [66.6,63.4,64.7]; x=1646 [49.5,52.9,56.6]; x=1899 [50.8,54.5,57.3]; x=2152 [57.7,54.0,54.4]; x=2405 [47.0,50.5,51.6]. Six of the nine non-lantern boxes have B > R, by 4.3 to 7.1 code values. A vertical column at x=1519 from y=644 to y=1135 gives luma p50 66.7, 65.8, 42.1, 39.6, 36.9, 36.4, 32.4 — the whole ground sits in a 32-67 window with no lit/shadow differentiation anywhere, while the distant mountains in the same frame read p50 162.8 warm [185.4,166.2,151.0]. The sun is plainly reaching the far terrain and contributing nothing measurable to the plateau. Whole-frame saturation is 0.178 and p1 is 17.9 — the lowest saturation and the only frame in the set without true blacks.
findings.why: The palette in ARCHITECTURE 5 is a warm key at #ffd9a8 -> #ff9b52 against a cool #4a6b8f fill. A ground plane that measures cooler than neutral under that key means the frame has one light, and it is the fill. That is why `wide` reads as an overcast afternoon with lanterns on, not as magic hour, and why it is the weakest frame on the contact sheet by a wide margin.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 15 already established the number that bounds this: with `this.rim` included, fill measures 0.5937 luminous irradiance against key 0.3960, so key/fill = 0.67 and the best achievable lit:shadow contrast is 1 + key/fill = 1.67x against 1.38x measured. If that still holds, the ceiling is an exposure-ratio problem, not a shadowing problem. DO NOT re-open cascade coverage, cascade weights, the caster set, or PCSS — rounds 7, 8 and 15 disproved all four, three separate times for the plaza specifically, and the standing instruction is that nobody touches cascade code for this. Verify the current key/fill ratio by ablation before changing anything.
findings.fix: Restore a visible key on the plateau in the `wide` framing. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: of the nine non-lantern boxes in the row `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png <x>,0.62,0.04,0.03` at x-frac 0.05/0.15/0.25/0.35/0.55/0.65/0.75/0.85/0.95, at least seven must have R > B by >= 6 code values (currently six of nine have B > R). Separately the frame must acquire lit/shadow structure: the p50 spread across those nine boxes must be >= 45 code values (currently 44.2 to 65.9 = 21.7). GUARD against faking with a global warm grade or exposure lift: whole-frame `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0,0,1,1` luma p50 must stay within +/-8% of its current 89.4, the sky control box `0.93,0.03,0.05,0.04` must stay within +/-5% per channel of its current [144.8,157.7,159.4] and must NOT go warm (it must keep B > R), and the mountain control `0.35,0.10,0.08,0.06` must stay within +/-8% per channel of [185.4,166.2,151.0].

findings.problem: The valley floor is a scatter test, not a field. At native the entire mid-ground is bare dirt carrying isolated single grass sprigs of two or three blades each, spaced roughly 40-60 px apart in a near-regular lattice, with essentially no ground cover between them and no clumping variation. Under every sprig sits an identical dark elliptical smudge, all the same size, aspect and orientation, tiling the whole field. Measured: a vertical run of 30x10 boxes at x=260 from y=620 to y=800 gives luma p50 70.8, 77.6, 85.3, 76.3, 85.3, 88.1, 89.0, 76.4, 89.0, 73.7, 69.5, 69.0, 66.8, 94.0, 40.4, 89.7, 80.5, 36.4, 97.7 — the ovals are 2.3-2.7x darker than the bare dirt between them (40.4 and 36.4 against 94.0 and 97.7) on a ~30 px vertical period. Crop to see the lattice: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-valley-r16.png 0.02,0.42,0.30,0.28`, and at 1:1 `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-valley-r16.png 0.06,0.55,0.10,0.09`.
findings.why: The regular repeat is the single loudest 'procedurally scattered' tell in the whole review set, and it covers about a third of the frame. Tsushima's golden-hour fields are the reference image for this project and they are dense, clumped, and gust-driven; a lattice of lone blades each sitting on an identical dark oval reads as debug scatter. It also makes ARCHITECTURE 5.5 unreachable — there is not enough grass on screen for a gust wavefront to be visible in it.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Two candidates: (a) the ground-cover density is low enough that the scatter's underlying grid is not being hidden by overlap, so the placement jitter is visible as a lattice; (b) the dark oval is a per-instance ground-contact darkening (AO card, contact decal, or vertex-AO disc) applied at a fixed size regardless of instance size, so every instance stamps the same shape. Verify which by ablating the oval alone and re-measuring the same vertical profile.
findings.fix: Make the field read as ground cover, not as instances. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: (1) the per-instance dark ovals must stop being a repeat — on the same vertical run of 30x10 boxes at x-frac 0.0987, y-frac 620/1170 to 800/1170 step 10 px, the ratio (max p50) / (min p50) must fall below 1.6 (currently 97.7/36.4 = 2.68). (2) Coverage must rise: `probe stats shots/phone-valley-rN.png 0.10,0.55,0.06,0.03` must return detail >= 16.0 (currently 11.14) and `0.10,0.42,0.06,0.03` must return detail >= 9.0 (currently 5.19), which is what real density does to mean |Laplacian| at this scale. GUARD against faking with a blur or a global contrast cut: the region mean must hold — box 0.10,0.55,0.06,0.03 meanRGB must stay within +/-8% per channel of its current [126.8,84.5,49.7], box 0.10,0.42,0.06,0.03 within +/-8% of [116.5,84.1,59.9], and whole-frame luma p50 within +/-6% of 83.0.

findings.problem: The shot named `valley` contains no valley. The ground runs dead flat from the foreground deck to a wall of trees at the horizon: no drop-off, no stream or water surface anywhere in the set (ARCHITECTURE 9 puts WATER_LEVEL 30 m below the plateau), no layered receding ridges, no mist, and no bamboo sea — the bamboo is a thin fringe of spindly culms at the tree line, not a sea. The frame therefore has exactly three depth planes (foreground railing, flat dirt, tree wall) and no aerial-perspective ladder between them. ARCHITECTURE 5 states the setting as 'a mountain shrine above a bamboo sea at magic hour... Mist in the valley', and this is the only framing in the review set that is supposed to show it.
findings.why: This is the establishing image of the game's premise and it delivers none of it. The reason Tsushima's vistas work is a legible vertical drop with three or four hazed depth bands stacked in it; a flat terrace to a tree wall has no depth to read, so the frame has nothing to say beyond its foreground.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING, AND DISPROVE THIS ONE FIRST BEFORE TOUCHING THE HEIGHTFIELD. The camera may simply not be aimed over the drop — in that case the heightfield is innocent and the fix is a pose change, not terrain. Ray-march or otherwise sample the terrain height along the `valley` view ray before concluding: if the surface under the ray is within a few metres of PLATEAU_HEIGHT all the way to the tree line, the terrain genuinely has no valley there; if it drops toward WATER_LEVEL outside the frustum, report that and hand the finding back rather than reshaping terrain. Round 15's lesson about SHOTS.sun applies directly — a stale pose was blamed on the wrong owner for several rounds.
findings.fix: Whichever of the two it turns out to be, the acceptance target is on the frame. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: the `valley` framing must contain at least three distinguishable depth bands with monotonically falling saturation and rising luma toward the horizon. Concretely, three boxes down the left third — `probe stats shots/phone-valley-rN.png 0.10,0.72,0.06,0.03` (near), `0.10,0.55,0.06,0.03` (mid), `0.10,0.42,0.06,0.03` (far) — currently read saturation 0.642 / 0.603 / 0.480 and p50 67.8 / 90.9 / 85.7, which is not monotone in luma. They must become monotone in both: saturation strictly falling with a near-to-far drop >= 0.30, and luma p50 strictly rising with a near-to-far rise >= 45. In addition a fourth, further band must exist below the tree line at `0.10,0.36,0.06,0.02` with saturation below the far band's by >= 0.08. GUARD: whole-frame luma p50 must stay within +/-8% of 83.0 and whole-frame saturation within +/-0.05 of 0.390, so this cannot be satisfied by a global haze or desaturation pass.

findings.problem: The distant mountain occupying the left quarter of the `torii` frame has no surface structure. Box (152,328 152x70) on the sunlit face reads detail 1.93 with lumaSpread 17.8; (253,234 127x59) on the snow cap reads detail 1.91; (430,421 152x59) on the lower slope reads 3.01. Crop `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-torii-r16.png 0.02,0.15,0.24,0.28` shows a smooth airbrushed dome with faint vertical streaking and no couloirs, no rock bands, no ridge lines, and no separation between snow and rock beyond a soft gradient.
findings.why: It is a large, high-contrast mass in the frame's negative space and it reads as painted backdrop rather than a mountain 2 km away. Sekiro's Ashina peaks and Tsushima's ranges both carry legible ridge and gully structure at this apparent size.
findings.fix: Add macro relief to the far heightfield so the silhouette and the shading both carry ridge/gully structure. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM frame: `probe stats shots/phone-torii-rN.png 0.06,0.28,0.06,0.06` must return detail >= 4.5 (currently 1.93) and lumaSpread >= 40 (currently 17.8), and `0.10,0.20,0.05,0.05` must return detail >= 4.0 (currently 1.91). GUARD against faking with noise or sharpening: both boxes' meanRGB must stay within +/-6% per channel of their current [144.0,131.2,126.2] and [193.1,179.4,163.2], the sky control box `0.70,0.18,0.08,0.04` must keep detail below 1.0 (currently 0.58), and whole-frame detail on `torii` must stay within +/-20% of its current 4.44.

notesOnApparatus: Every number in this review came from tools/probe.mjs. No custom measurement code was written this round, so the recurring 3-channel-PNG / 4-byte-stride bug had no opportunity to recur. `detail` was used only for fine texture (post grain, canopy petals, mountain relief); for the two low-frequency questions — god-ray shafts and the sky gradient — I used explicit profiles (an arc of 16x16 boxes at r=330 px around the sun disc, and vertical/horizontal runs of boxes) and quoted the sequences, per the round-15 apparatus note that `detail` cannot see a shaft. CANDIDATES KILLED BY MEASUREMENT, DO NOT RE-FILE: (1) 'the wide mid-distance forest band is high-contrast acid-green clip-art' — my eye read it that way at native, but probing killed it: lit tree (161,354 20x20) p50 99.6 sat 0.155, dark tree (281,329) p50 90.4 sat 0.122, bare dirt (317,414) p50 100.5 sat 0.145. The whole band lives in a 10-code window and aerial perspective is working there. Not filed. (2) 'stair-stepped mountain ridgeline in torii' — visible in a 608x328 crop, but at 152x70 1:1 (`crop 0.085,0.175,0.06,0.06`) the summit edge is clean, and round 8 already disproved the wide ridgeline silhouette with a 72 px longest straight run. Not filed. (3) 'black speck debris around the valley bamboo leaf tufts' — round 8's luma-only detector already killed that population at 2/2/0/0/0 genuinely detached specks; I did not re-test it and did not file it. (4) 'sky banding' — per-box lumaSpread 3.9-4.8 and detail 0.39-0.76 across the hero and torii sky columns; the ramp is smooth and round 15 confirmed it is cleanly dithered under a 16x stretch. Not filed; the sky finding here is about chroma and gradient range, not banding. (5) 'no cast shadows on the plaza / no cast shadows in wide' — deliberately NOT filed. Rounds 7, 8 and 15 disproved this three separate times, including a case where the critic's own 'shaded plaza' box was 84.6% cast shadow, and the standing instruction is that nobody touches cascade code for it. The `wide` finding above is filed as an exposure-ratio symptom (ground measures net blue under a warm key) and explicitly tells the owner not to re-open cascades. (6) The hero blob's identity as a puddle was tested and rejected on physics, not on code: a wet-stone puddle under a sky at luma 165-190 cannot read RGB [2.9,3.0,4.0]. The sun disc used as the arc centre was located from the pixels at (1528,538), which agrees with round 15's independently measured (0.604,0.453) to within the disc's own radius.
